title: What Happens When You Crack Your Knuckles?
sources: Swanson, S. C. (2014). Knuckle cracking and hand function.
Castellini, C., & Wilke, H. (1994). The effects of passive joint manipulation on joint stability.

lines.text: You know that satisfying crack when you bend your fingers?
lines.caps: YOU KNOW THAT *SATISFYING | CRACK WHEN YOU *BEND | YOUR *FINGERS

lines.text: But what is actually happening inside your joint?
Your knuckles are full of synovial fluid, a natural lubricant.
lines.caps: YOUR *KNUCKLES | ARE FULL OF *SYNOVIAL | FLUID, A *NATURAL

lines.text: It keeps your bones moving smoothly without grinding.
When you crack your knuckles, you are stretching the joint.
lines.caps: WHEN YOU *CRACK | YOUR KNUCKLES, | YOU ARE *STRETCHING

lines.text: That pop sound is a bubble of gas forming in the fluid.
lines.caps: THAT *POP SOUND IS | A *BUBBLE | OF GAS *FORMING

lines.text: Nitrogen and carbon dioxide rush in, creating a vacuum pocket.
lines.caps: NITROGEN AND *CARBON | DIOXIDE *RUSH IN | CREATING A *VACUUM

lines.text: So does cracking cause arthritis? No, that is a total myth.
lines.caps: SO DOES *CRACKING | CAUSE *ARTHRITIS | *NO, THAT IS A *TOTAL

lines.text: Your cartilage is tough and is not worn down by this.
But if you crack them nonstop, all day, every day...
You might irritate the joint or weaken your grip over time.
lines.caps: YOU MIGHT *IRRITATE | THE *JOINT OR | WEAKEN YOUR *GRIP

lines.text: So maybe, just do not overdo it.
